notes:
Background: PayTrailor is a mid-market payments SaaS that integrates with Stripe + Zuora for subscription billing. Their support org (120 agents) wants a chat+agent layer to handle billing inquiries, plan changes, refunds and rerouting to Zuora workflows.

What they told us (on 2026-01-12 demo):
- "We need reliable streaming responses for multi-step refunds — agents hate waiting for full model completion."
- Wants JSON structured outputs for downstream automation (normalize into Zuora API payloads).
- Must support tool-calling: call Stripe/Zuora connectors, confirm actions, then return structured audit-friendly JSON.

Technical constraints / targets:
- Latency SLO: end-to-end 300-500ms token latency for first-chunk streaming on typical chat flow; tail < 1s for agent-facing interactions.
- Throughput target during peak: ~2k concurrent agent sessions, average 10 tokens/sec sustained per session during escalations.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget; optimizing batching and prefix caching important.
- Model preferences: prefer open/Redwood-verified models; want ability to pin and fallback to smaller quantized variants during cost-sensitive hours.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, and per-request audit ID required for compliance.

Recent timeline (high level):
- 2026-01-12: Hosted API demo + streaming sample with mock Stripe calls (Jamie, Samir, PayTrailor product).
- 2026-01-20: Security questionnaire submitted; waiting on legal review (see linked_drive_docs).
- 2026-02-10: POC kickoff — goal: 2-week POC for hosted API with live Stripe sandbox integration, structured JSON outputs to feed Zuora patch jobs. (SE + PayTrailor infra).
- 2026-02-14: Observability workshop; asked for traceable request IDs and retention policy options.
- 2026-02-15: Initial streaming latency test results — 1st-chunk median 320ms on hosted; tail p95 ~820ms. Customer asked for 20% improvement to meet stricter SLOs.

POC scope and success criteria (customer-proposed):
- End-to-end agent flow that: recognizes billing intent, calls Stripe sandbox via tool call, generates validated JSON payload for Zuora, logs audit entry.
- Streaming first-chunk <= 300ms median on customer's simulated network.
- Fallback behavior: when capacity constrained, degrade to smaller quantized model without loss of required JSON fields.
- Per-request cost metric visible in Redwood Console and ability to set cost cap alerts.

Sales/Commercial notes:
- Primary ask: start on Hosted API POC. If POC meets latency + security bar, move to Dedicated (reserved capacity) for production with burst capacity option.
- Price sensitivity around committed throughput vs burst. They asked for a modeled cost comparison (hosted vs dedicated) for 2k concurrent sessions and 10% monthly growth. (Jamie to deliver by 2026-02-25).

Quotes / direct lines:
- Product lead: "We can't block agents for 2-3 seconds waiting for model to finish — streaming is non-negotiable."
- CTO: "Auditability + structured output wins this. If the model can generate reliable JSON and we can call Zuora safely, it's a go."

Action items (owner -> due):
- Jamie: deliver hosted vs dedicated cost model + TCO scenarios (2026-02-25).
- Samir: run quantized-model latency tests + propose kernel/config tweaks for <300ms first-chunk (2026-02-22).
- PayTrailor infra: complete legal security review; confirm accepted KMS provider and residency constraints (in progress).

Short next-step (sales): schedule technical deep-dive with infra + security to finalize POC acceptance criteria and sign-off timeline.
